registry.description: Disobedience is the refusal to do what one has been commanded — a straightforward act of the will that sets itself against authority. The Greek vocabulary here is precise: the word covers both the failure to listen and the active decision not to comply. In the New Testament it is used to describe humanity's fundamental condition apart from God (disobedience to his word and ways) as well as the specific acts that express it. Disobedience is always relational: it is not breaking a rule in the abstract but refusing the one who gave the command.
